sections.title: Klasifikasi Tumor Otak

content.text: Brain tumors are classified by: ORIGIN (primary CNS tumors vs metastatic); LOCATION (intra-axial within brain parenchyma vs extra-axial outside brain tissue); HISTOLOGY (WHO classification grades I-IV). PRIMARY CNS TUMORS: Gliomas arise from glial cells - astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, ependymoma, glioblastoma. Meningiomas from arachnoid cap cells. Pituitary adenomas. Schwannomas (vestibular). Primary CNS lymphoma. METASTATIC BRAIN TUMORS: Most common brain tumors in adults; typically multiple; sources: lung (40-50%), breast (15-20%), melanoma (10%), kidney, colon. WHO GRADING: Grade I (benign, slow-growing, curable with surgery); Grade II (low-grade, infiltrative, may recur); Grade III (anaplastic, malignant); Grade IV (highly malignant, rapid growth, necrosis).

sections.title: Presentasi Klinis

content.text: GENERAL SYMPTOMS (increased ICP): Headache (progressive, worse in morning, with coughing/straining/Valsalva), nausea and vomiting (often projectile, worse in morning), papilledema (blurred vision, transient visual obscurations), altered mental status (cognitive slowing, personality changes, somnolence), seizures (may be presenting symptom in 20-40% of brain tumors). FOCAL SYMPTOMS (depend on location): Frontal (personality changes, executive dysfunction, hemiparesis); Temporal (memory deficits, seizures, aphasia); Parietal (sensory loss, neglect, apraxia, Gerstmann syndrome); Occipital (visual field defects); Posterior fossa (ataxia, cranial nerve deficits, hydrocephalus); Brainstem (cranial nerve palsies, long tract signs). PITUITARY/SELLAR: Visual field defects (bitemporal hemianopia), endocrine abnormalities.
Gejala umum: nyeri kepala pagi hari, muntah, papiledema
Kejang: gejala awal pada 20-40% tumor otak
Morning headache that worsens with Valsalva is classic for raised ICP from mass lesion

sections.title: Tumor Primer

content.text: GLIOBLASTOMA MULTIFORME (GBM, WHO Grade IV): Most common malignant primary brain tumor in adults; peak age 45-70; highly infiltrative; MRI shows irregular ring-enhancing mass with central necrosis, extensive edema, mass effect, may cross corpus callosum. Treatment: maximal safe resection + concurrent chemoradiation (temozolomide + RT) + adjuvant temozolomide; median survival 15 months. MENINGIOMA (WHO Grade I-III): Most common benign brain tumor; female predominance; extra-axial, dural-based, homogeneous enhancement, dural tail sign; treatment: observation if small/asymptomatic, surgery if symptomatic or growing, radiosurgery for residual/recurrent. PITUITARY ADENOMA: Sellar mass; microadenoma (<10mm) or macroadenoma (>=10mm); visual field defects if suprasellar extension; treatment: medical (prolactinoma - cabergoline/bromocriptine), transsphenoidal surgery, radiation. SCHWANNOMA (VESTIBULAR SCHWANNOMA, ACOUSTIC NEUROMA): CPA mass from vestibular nerve; unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance; MRI shows enhancing CPA mass extending into IAC; treatment: observation if small, surgery or radiosurgery if growing/symptomatic. PRIMARY CNS LYMPHOMA: Periventricular, homogeneous enhancement, restricted diffusion; treatment: high-dose methotrexate-based chemotherapy.

sections.title: Tumor Metastasis

content.text: Metastatic brain tumors are the most common brain tumors in adults. Typically multiple lesions at gray-white matter junction. Common primary sources: lung (40-50%), breast (15-20%), melanoma (10%), renal cell carcinoma, colorectal. MRI: multiple lesions with ring or homogeneous enhancement, disproportionate surrounding edema compared to tumor size. Hemorrhagic metastases: melanoma, renal cell, cholangiocarcinoma, thyroid, lung. WORKUP: Chest CT (most common source), mammography, abdominal CT, tumor markers. TREATMENT: Depends on number, size, location, primary tumor type, KPS score. Single/few accessible: surgical resection or SRS (stereotactic radiosurgery). Multiple: whole brain radiation therapy (WBRT). Systemic therapy for chemosensitive tumors. Prognosis: RPA class I (KPS >=70, age <65, controlled primary, no extracranial mets) = median 7.7 months; Class III (KPS <70) = median 2 months.
Multiple brain lesions at gray-white junction with known primary cancer = metastases until proven otherwise

sections.title: Prinsip Manajemen

content.text: SURGERY: Indications - accessible lesion causing mass effect, need for histological diagnosis, single metastasis, recurrent/residual after other treatment. Goals: maximal safe resection while preserving function (awake craniotomy for eloquent areas). RADIATION THERAPY: Whole brain RT (WBRT) for multiple metastases; Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS/Gamma Knife) for 1-4 small metastases or residual tumor; Fractionated RT for gliomas; Proton beam for selected cases. CHEMOTHERAPY: Temozolomide for gliomas; Methotrexate for primary CNS lymphoma; Targeted therapy (bevacizumab for GBM). SYMPTOMATIC MANAGEMENT: Corticosteroids (dexamethasone 4-10 mg q6h) for vasogenic edema - taper after definitive treatment; Antiepileptics (levetiracetam, valproate) only if seizures have occurred (not for prophylaxis); PPI for GI protection with steroids; DVT prophylaxis; Pain management.
Simtomatik: deksametason 4-10 mg q6h, antiepileptik jika kejang
Prophylactic antiepileptics are NOT recommended for brain tumors without seizure history

diagnostic_logic.title: Clinical suspicion
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Progressive headache, focal deficits, seizures, personality changes

diagnostic_logic.title: MRI with contrast
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Gold standard; assess number, location, enhancement pattern, edema

diagnostic_logic.title: Tissue diagnosis if needed
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Biopsy or resection for histology and molecular markers

diagnostic_logic.title: Staging for metastases
diagnostic_logic.explanation: CT chest/abdomen, mammography, tumor markers to find primary

differential_notes.how_to_separate: GBM: single, irregular ring, crosses corpus callosum; Metastasis: multiple, gray-white junction; Abscess: thin smooth ring, restricted diffusion center
Meningioma: extra-axial, dural tail, broad dural base; Schwannoma: CPA, extends into IAC
Adenoma: solid, homogenous; Craniopharyngioma: cystic, calcified, suprasellar

treatment_notes.content: Maximal safe resection for accessible tumors; biopsy for diagnosis
WBRT for multiple mets, SRS for 1-4 mets, fractionated RT for gliomas
Temozolomide for gliomas, methotrexate for lymphoma
Dexamethasone for edema, antiepileptics if seizures, DVT prophylaxis

red_flags: Seizure in adult with no prior history
Multiple brain lesions with known cancer
